notes: GROUPING: one long sentence; the subject 'dūtaḥ' comes near the end (dūto vaidyam upasarpan aśubhaḥ). The giant compound 'tṛṇa...sneha-bhājana-dharaḥ' is printed as one word ending in -dharaḥ (bearer, holder) and is rendered as a list in the printed order; the body parts inside it (head, nose, ..., lower leg) sit oddly with 'bearer', and 'spṛk' (possibly 'touching') suggests the original may have listed things touched, but this is not certain and no verb is supplied. The printed 'loṣṭupāṃgāra' is read as loṣṭa + aṅgāra (charcoal), which does not match the print letter for letter (the letters 'u' and 'pā' are dropped; loṣṭa + pāṃsu 'dust' + aṅgāra is another possible guess), and 'mārjanośastra' as mārjana + ūṣa (saline soil) + śastra; both are conjectural. 'pala' is flesh (pala can also be a measure); 'kapāla' skull or potsherd. 'pādābhyāṃ bhuvaṃ muñcan' is rendered literally, its sense is unclear. 'vyādhino' is a doubtful form (vyādhin nominative would be vyādhī); read as 'diseased'. 'neko' (before jīrṇa) has a visarga-o for which the compound gives no reason; 'aneka' is rendered 'of many kinds'. notes: GROUPING: one long list governed by 'prasthāna-gamana-praveśeṣu' and ending with the summary 'etad aṣṭottaraṃ maṅgalānāṃ śataṃ ... diśanti'; no verb is stated before 'diśanti', and the list items are nominatives understood as the auspicious things met at setting out. The count of items was not reconciled with the stated 108. Identifications: udumbara = Ficus racemosa, cluster fig (standard); aśvattha = Ficus religiosa, peepal (standard); siddhārthaka = white mustard, Brassica/Sinapis alba (probable); rocanā = gorocanā, the yellow pigment from the cow (probable); haridrā = turmeric, Curcuma longa (standard); vacā = sweet flag, Acorus calamus (standard); priyaṅgu = Callicarpa macrophylla (probable; other plants proposed, disputed); cāṣa = Indian roller or blue jay, Coracias benghalensis (probable); kīcaka = hollow bamboo that whistles in the wind (probable). 'kuśadarśa' is read as kuśa + ādarśa (mirror) conjecturally. 'vaṃruṇa' before madhu is unclear and left unsplit; 'madhumadasikta' is read as madhu-mada-sikta, sense of 'honey-rut' uncertain. 'abudaḥ' is read as ambudaḥ (cloud). 'phalānyārdre' is read as phalāni + ārdram (fresh) agreeing with māṃsam, conjecturally. 'dharmārthakāmāmāśritam' has an extra 'mā' and is read dharma-artha-kāma-āśritam. 'vardhamāna' (increasing, or an auspicious emblem) and 'mānuṣam' are rendered literally. kṣamā is forbearance (or earth). 'sravantyaḥ' (flowing ones) = rivers. hindi: पुरुष नाम वाले पक्षी बाईं ओर शुभ हैं; शिवा यानी सम्भवतः सियारिन, श्यामा, पिंगला, कोकिला, अस्पष्ट शब्द रला, छुछुन्दरी यानी छछूंदर, सूकरी यानी मादा सूअर, घर की छिपकली और एक खुर वाले पशु, स्त्री नाम वाले, दाहिनी ओर शुभ हैं; मोर, भालू, श्रीकण्ठ और कुत्ता, ऐसा, नहीं; हाथी, बकरा और पयस् यानी दूध या जल भी; प्रवेश के समय ये उलटे हैं। और सब जगह अनुमानित पाठ पर कुत्ते और सियार का दाहिने से बाईं ओर जाना अनिष्ट है; मृग और पक्षियों का उलटा है।
english: Birds with male names, on the left, are auspicious; śivā (probably the she-jackal), śyāmā, piṅgalā, kokilā (cuckoo), an unclear word (ralā), the musk shrew (chuchundarī), the sow, the house lizard and single-hoofed animals, having female names, are auspicious on the right; the peacock, bear, śrīkaṇṭha and dog, thus, not; the elephant, the goat and payas (milk or water) also; but at entering they are reversed. And everywhere, on a conjectural reading, the going of a dog and a jackal from the right to the left is undesired; the reverse for beasts and birds.

words.gloss: in nodules (granthi), tumours (arbuda) and so on
in gulma (abdominal lump), udara (abdominal disease; probable) and so on
in diarrhoea (atisāra), raktapitta (a bleeding disorder) and so on
in urinary stone (aśmarī), udāvarta (upward-turning of wind) and so on

hindi: इसी प्रकार ग्रन्थि यानी गाँठ और अर्बुद यानी रसौली आदि में छेद शब्द इष्ट है; गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ और उदर यानी सम्भवतः पेट का रोग आदि में भेद शब्द; अतिसार यानी दस्त और रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव का रोग आदि में रुद्ध शब्द; अश्मरी यानी पथरी और उदावर्त यानी वायु का ऊपर की ओर पलटना आदि में प्रवर्तन शब्द, ऐसा।
english: Likewise, in granthi (nodule), arbuda (tumour) and the like, the word 'cutting' (cheda) is desired; in gulma (abdominal lump), udara (probably an abdominal disease) and the like, the word 'breaking' (bheda); in atisāra (diarrhoea), raktapitta (a bleeding disorder) and the like, the word 'stopped' (ruddha); in aśmarī (urinary stone), udāvarta (upward-turning of wind) and the like, the word 'impelling' (pravartana): thus.
notes: 'iṣṭaḥ' is stated once and carried to the later pairs (elliptical; no verb supplied). Identifications: granthi = nodule or cyst, arbuda = tumour (standard); gulma = abdominal lump (probable); udara here is the abdominal disease (probably the swelling of the belly), not the belly itself (probable); atisāra = diarrhoea (standard); raktapitta = a bleeding disorder (standard); aśmarī = urinary stone (standard); udāvarta = a disorder in which the downward wind is turned upward, with stoppage of stool and wind (probable). 'chedaśabdaiṣṭo' (छेदशब्दइष्टो) and 'pravarttanaśabdaiti' (प्रवर्त्तनशब्दइति) are printed with separate vowels: regular hiatus after -aḥ (śabda iṣṭaḥ, śabda iti), not typos. The doubled -rtt- of pravarttana is normalised (recorded once book-wide).

of a thorn, one with raised foot, vehicle, bed, seat and so on, broken, household articles, empty pot, madya (an intoxicating drink), fat (vasā), oil, a pregnant woman, a śvapāka (dog-cooker, outcaste), one in distress (vyasanin), the dead

hindi: छींक, मारा गया, गिरा, चीख, प्रहार, छेद, भेद, जलना, हाहा और निषेध आदि शब्द निषिद्ध हैं; निषिद्ध और जलती हुई दिशा में पक्षियों और पशुओं की क्रूर ध्वनियाँ; या सूखे और मुरझाए, लताओं और काँटों वाले वृक्ष पर अथवा वैसे ही स्थान में; और तृण, पलल यानी कीचड़ या मांस या तिल की लुगदी, लकड़ी का बोझ, ठीकरा, ढेला आदि का, काँटे का, ऊपर उठे पैर वाले का, वाहन, शय्या, आसन आदि का, टूटा हुआ, गृहसामग्री, खाली घड़ा, मद्य यानी नशीला पेय, वसा, तेल, गर्भिणी, श्वपाक, विपत्ति में पड़े हुए और मृतों का दर्शन, प्रवेश के समय; और रोगी के घर से पहले कहे गए मंगल पदार्थों का निकलना, अनुमानित पाठ पर; और भीतर आए वैद्य का सत्कार नहीं, लाभ, सन्तोष और स्तुतियाँ, रोगी के शुभ और अशुभ; अनुमानित पाठ पर, वक्र और अनुवक्र ग्रह, निन्दित स्थानों में स्थित; केतु, शनि और राहु द्वारा जन्म नक्षत्र का दबाया जाना; घर, पत्नी, शय्या, आसन, वाहन, मणि, रत्न और उपकरणों में निन्दित लक्षणों का प्रकट होना, चिकित्सा के निषेध के लिए।
english: The words sneeze (kṣuta), struck, fallen, outcry, blow, cutting, breaking, burning, 'hā hā', prohibition and the like are forbidden; in a forbidden and in a blazing direction, cruel cries of birds and beasts; or on a dry, withered tree with creepers and thorns, or in a place of that kind; and, at the entering, the sight of grass, palala (sense uncertain: mud, flesh or sesame paste), a bundle of wood, a potsherd, a clod and so on, of a thorn, of one with raised foot, of vehicles, beds, seats and so on, broken, household articles, empty pots, madya (an intoxicating drink), fat (vasā), oil, a pregnant woman, a śvapāka (dog-cooker, outcaste), one in distress (vyasanin) and the dead; and, on a conjectural reading, the going out of the previously mentioned auspicious things from the patient's house; and for the physician who has entered, no honour, and gain, satisfaction and praises, auspicious and inauspicious (ones) of the patient; on a conjectural reading, the planets (graha) retrograde and following-retrograde (vakra, anuvakra), standing in condemned positions; the overpowering of the birth-nakṣatra by Ketu, Saturn and Rāhu; or the appearance of condemned signs in house, wife, bed, seat, vehicle, gem, jewel, equipment: for the prohibition of treatment.

possible: stray r (lābhaḥ tuṣṭi would give lābhastuṣṭi)
possible: 'yahā' for 'grahāḥ' (gra/ya confusion), since garhitasthānasthāḥ (nom. pl.) follows

notes: GROUPING: one very long sentence of lists; the only predicate is 'pratiṣiddhāḥ' (forbidden) in the first clause, and the rest is read as a series of omen-lists ending in 'cikitsāpratiṣedhāya' (for the prohibition of treatment, i.e. for refusing the case); no verb is supplied and the reading is low confidence. The close of the list of items seen ('tṛṇa ... mṛtānām') is read as a genitive of 'darśanam'. 'bhagna' probably qualifies the preceding yāna, śayana and āsana; 'ūrdhvapāda' may mean one standing on tiptoe or with raised feet; printed 'orddha' has a doubled dd (normalised). 'palala' has several senses (mud, flesh, sesame paste): disputed here. 'śvapāka' = outcaste, lit. dog-cooker. 'cāturgṛhāt' is read ca + āturagṛhāt (patient's house) conjecturally, and 'pūrvīkta' as pūrvokta (previously mentioned), the auspicious things being those of unit 10; 'lābhartuṣṭi' has a stray r. 'śubhāśubhā āturasya' (auspicious and inauspicious of the patient) attaches either to the preceding lābha-tuṣṭi-nutayaḥ or opens the next clause; kept literal. 'vakrānuvakrāyahā' is read vakra-anuvakrāḥ grahāḥ (vakra = retrograde motion of a planet; anuvakra = a later retrograde stage; probable), conjecturally. 'ketuśini rāhubhiḥ' is read ketu-śani-rāhubhiḥ, the compound divided by a printed space. 'savallikaṃṭake' read sa-vallika-kaṇṭake.

words.gloss: cause of the auspicious and the inauspicious

hindi: स्वप्न स्वयं या दूसरे के द्वारा देखा गया शुभ और अशुभ का कारण है। वह सात प्रकार का है: देखा हुआ, सुना हुआ, अनुभव किया हुआ, चाहा हुआ, कल्पित, भाविक यानी आगे होने वाले से सम्बन्धित, और दोषों से उत्पन्न।
english: A dream, seen by oneself or by another, is a cause of the auspicious and the inauspicious. It is of seven kinds: seen, heard, experienced, desired, imagined, bhāvika (relating to what will be), and born of the doṣas.

'bhāvika' is rendered literally (a dream of what is to come); the Sanskrit gives no more. The seven kinds are named in order; the next unit says the first five are fruitless.

words.gloss: according to one's own natural constitution (prakṛti)
in the first part of the night

hindi: उनमें पहले पाँच प्रकार निष्फल हैं; इसी प्रकार जो अपनी प्रकृति के अनुसार है, जो भूल गया, जो दिन में देखा गया, बहुत छोटा, बहुत लम्बा, और जो गहरी नींद में नहीं देखा गया; रात्रि के पहले भाग में वह थोड़ा और देर से फल देता है।
english: Among these, the first five kinds are fruitless; likewise (one) according to one's own natural constitution (prakṛti), forgotten, by day, too short, too long, and seen when not deeply asleep; in the first part of the night it gives a little fruit, and after a long time.
notes: Elliptical: after 'tathā' the list (own prakṛti, forgotten, by day, too short, too long, not seen in deep sleep) has no stated predicate; it is read as parallel to 'aphalaḥ' (fruitless), but the text does not say so and the last clause ('pūrvarātre ... phalaṃ karoti') has its own verb. 'nātisuptadṛṣṭaḥ' could also be read 'seen not when very asleep' (as rendered) or as a compound of 'not too deeply asleep'. 'ādyaḥ pañcavidhaḥ' = the first five of the seven kinds in unit 20 (seen, heard, experienced, desired, imagined).
